anna: Deploying a Cloudflare Worker that imports our SDK fails with "require is not defined" and a big buffer polyfill pulled in. Anyone have a compact fix?

kevin: Two practical fixes: (A) add an explicit edge entrypoint e.g. `@redwood/inference-js/edge` that only uses web APIs, or (B) keep one package but guard node-only code behind dynamic imports so bundlers don't include it.

shreya: For (A) we use package.json exports like: `"./edge": { "import": "./dist/index.edge.mjs" }` and a `browser`/`default` condition for the main entry. Consumers can `import '.../edge'` to be explicit.

kevin: Also avoid core node types in top-level d.ts. Set `types: ./dist/index.d.ts` that is runtime-agnostic. If you need node-specific types, add `index.node.d.ts`.

shreya: For Buffer/base64 on edge implement tiny helpers: `const b64ToBytes = s => Uint8Array.from(atob(s), c => c.charCodeAt(0))` and use Web Crypto (`crypto.subtle`) for HMAC. That avoids huge polyfills.

anna: Any quick esbuild/wrangler tips so people don't accidentally bundle CJS?

kevin: Build with `platform: 'browser'` and add a CI esbuild job that bundles `dist/index.edge.mjs` to catch accidental node imports. Also prefer conditional exports over main/module fields.

shreya: For retry/idempotency—expose options so callers can pass `retry: { retries: 0 }` and an `idempotencyHeader` (e.g., `x-idempotency-key`) so Workers can set a UUID per operation to prevent duplicate side effects on transient 520/524.

anna: OK actions: Kevin - PR for `/edge` entry + edge micro-shims; Shreya - doc snippet for wrangler/esbuild + TS guidance; I'll add CI bundle check. Thanks :thumbsup:
